dedupe_keys.name: grandi dighe italiane italian large dams list

description: Grandi dighe italiane is the open list of Italy's large dams published on the Ministry of Infrastructure and Transport's open data portal by its information systems and statistics directorate, drawing on the register kept by the Directorate General for Dams and Water Infrastructure, which supervises the safety of dams under state competence. Each row is a dam with its name, prevailing use such as irrigation, hydropower or drinking water, province and region, height and reservoir volume as defined by Law 584/1994, structural type such as earth or rockfill with a central core, and the years construction started and ended. Coverage is national for large dams under state supervision; the dataset's temporal extent ends on 1 March 2019 and the files were last updated on 4 March 2022, with an irregular update frequency. Data come as a small CSV and an Excel file, free under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0. Caveats: there are no coordinates, so dams must be located by name and province, smaller dams under regional competence are excluded, and the list may lag the directorate's current register, whose pages blocked our checking environment. Simulation uses: building a national dam inventory for dam-break hazard exposure and seismic risk screening, reservoir storage for irrigation and supply capacity planning, and age-based condition analysis using the construction years. Related records: the ICOLD World Register of Dams (data-icold-world-register-of-dams) and the US National Inventory of Dams (data-usace-national-inventory-of-dams) are comparable registers.
